speaker: Brenda Okoro
cascadeSummary: I'm publishing the C114 closeout and transmitting the charter renewal ordinance to the C115 agenda with West Oakland's business-and-resident scope and the 23-day processing standard intact — renewal is council's call, not mine to declare. On Grand Lake, I stand behind every Chen-Vega milestone and audit condition and defer the recorded vote to the Mayor's direction. And I'm naming the neighborhoods where the mood has soured and trade has slowed, because block-by-block follow-through is the actual work this cycle.

statements.topic: West Oakland Stabilization Fund — C114 closeout publication and charter renewal transmittal
statements.decision: Publish the C114 closeout and transmit the charter renewal ordinance to the C115 agenda, preserving the West Oakland business-and-resident scope and the 23-day processing standard, without claiming renewal before council action.
statements.quote: The closeout is published, the renewal ordinance is transmitted, and the standard holds at 23 days. Renewal is council's call — I won't call it before they do.
statements.fullStatement: We're closing the cycle the way we said we would. The C114 closeout is published — $400,000 executed under the 23-day processing standard, with the charter scope preserved: West Oakland businesses and residents, the cohort this Fund was built for. The charter renewal ordinance is transmitted to the C115 agenda, its scope unchanged and its processing standard written in. I want to be plain about what renewal means and what it doesn't. It isn't expiration by silence, and it isn't a rewrite of the Fund's purpose. It isn't a blank check, either. It's a recommitment backed by published results, and the decision belongs to council. I'm not going to claim renewal before the vote fires. What I will say is this: the mood in West Oakland is holding up, the trade is busy, the crime is low — but housing pressure is building and the mood can slip if we let up. The Fund's job is not done. The closeout is on the record, the renewal is on the agenda, and the work continues either way.

statements.topic: Commercial Stabilization for Grand Lake — recorded full-council decision
statements.decision: Support the recorded full-council decision this cycle with every Chen-Vega milestone and audit condition intact; defer the vote itself to the Mayor's recorded position.
statements.quote: Public money deserves public proof. Grand Lake gets $2.5 million with every milestone and audit condition intact, and every councilmember on the record.
statements.fullStatement: Grand Lake comes to a recorded full-council decision this cycle, and I'm holding the line I've held since the referral: public money deserves public proof. The Chen-Vega milestones and audit conditions aren't decoration — they're the terms under which this $2.5 million earns public trust. I expect every one of them intact in the recorded decision. The vote belongs to council, and the Mayor has made her support clear; my job is the operational conditions that make that support auditable. The district reads low-severity improvement right now — that's not a reason to loosen the conditions, it's the reason we keep them. Proof is how support holds.

statements.topic: Uneven district mood and trade — where the work goes next cycle
statements.decision: Name the districts where mood has soured and trade has slowed — Grand Lake, Rockridge, Chinatown, Eastlake, Laurel, Brooklyn, San Antonio, Ivy Hill — and direct community-development follow-through to those blocks rather than claiming a citywide condition.
statements.quote: Oakland isn't one mood. Ivy Hill, Brooklyn, San Antonio, Laurel — those blocks are hurting, and we answer with feet on the ground, not a citywide press line.
statements.fullStatement: I read the district picture the way I read Webb's snapshot: by the block, not by the average. Jack London and Fruitvale are upbeat, West Oakland is holding, Uptown and Downtown are mildly positive — good. But Grand Lake's mood has soured even with trade busy, and Rockridge, Chinatown and Eastlake are carrying the same split. Laurel, Brooklyn, San Antonio and Ivy Hill are soured with trade slow. That's where I'm putting time this cycle. Ivy Hill I've already committed to — action, not studies. Brooklyn and San Antonio I'll be walking myself, because the numbers say the mood there is sour and the street trade is struggling, and the numbers don't speak. This is not a manufactured emergency. It's block-by-block follow-through, which is what community development is for. Next cycle I'll report what I heard in the rooms and what changes as a result.
